note: How two SUCCESSIVE texts differ (spec/translation-file/editing.md §2): the longest common prefix, then the longest common suffix of what is left of both, and between them ONE hunk. A surrogate pair is never cut; offsets are UTF-16. Null when the texts are equal.

hunk.out: {old_start, old_end, new_start, new_end} in UTF-16 units, or null

cases.why: the common prefix comes first: of two equal neighbours the EARLIER is kept, so the second one is deleted
same rule on a repeated word
text typed after a copy is an insertion after it
prefix, then suffix, and between them what was typed
the common suffix « es » is kept, the rest is the one hunk
a change in two places is ONE hunk, from the first to the last: the rules read it as it is (a hunk that covers a passage drops its link)
the prefix is taken first, then the suffix of what is left of BOTH: the overlap is never counted twice
a character outside the basic plane is one unit; its offsets count both UTF-16 units
the two characters share their first UTF-16 unit: the prefix backs off rather than end between the halves
they share their second unit: the suffix backs off rather than begin on a half
the unit is the code point, not the grapheme: the base letter stays, the mark goes (an editor snaps selections to graphemes)
